title: Qdrant cutover complete: Rust Vector Engine is the canonical semantic index
summary: Executes the A610-declared cutover: every article that named Qdrant as canonical semantic index, formal tool, or live-path component now names the Rust Vector Engine (vectord, contract vectord/v1). A610 Qdrant status -> retired; A611 target-primary -> primary; A621 cutover sealed. Migration evidence: qdrant collection gptbridge_shared_knowledge holds 0 points and 0 aliases (allocated-but-empty segments), vectord schema re-created at identical 2560-dim cosine; consumer verification suite green. Source storage retained per DATA-SAFETY.
origin: codex-vs-implementation audit + live migration probe 2026-09-26; user directive: complete Rust takeover

problem.summary: A8/A44/A49/A52/A65/A191/A284/A365-A374/A387/A524/A549 and peers still declare Qdrant canonical/formal while the live path runs vectord (rust); A610/A611/A621 carry pre-cutover wording

AUTHORITY:PostgreSQL is central official mutable structured-data authority;SQLite is module-private bounded state and bounded degradation;Rust-Vector-Engine is rebuildable semantic projection. A SQLite outage may buffer locally but never promotes SQLite to central authority. PRIORITY-1-RECONCILIATION:every PostgreSQL<->SQLite governed record uses resource_id,revision,content_hash,sync_status,last_synced_at;sync_status enum is pending|syncing|synced|conflict|failed|stale. Compare revision+hash+authority provenance before mutation; conflict is isolated and evidence-preserved,never last-write-wins;retry is idempotent;successful reconciliation records both endpoints and correlation_id. PRIORITY-2-GLOBAL-ID:PostgreSQL,SQLite,Rust-Vector-Engine share one immutable resource_id and version contract;RAG additionally records chunk_id,rust-vector-engine_point_id,version,source_revision,content_hash,embedding_model/version and pipeline revision. Identifier mappings are centrally recoverable and cannot be synthesized independently by projections. PRIORITY-3-POSTGRES-INDEX:optimize measured canonical query families only:module_id+classification+status;logical_key+module_id;resource_relation source/target;tool_request status/target;central audit module/time. Every index requires query-plan evidence,write/storage budget and ownership;blanket per-column indexing is forbidden. PRIORITY-4-TRANSPORT:durable request queue envelope includes request_id,idempotency_key,status,target,lease_owner,lease_expires_at,retry_count,next_retry_at,timeout/deadline,correlation_id,last_error_class and dead-letter state. Processing requires atomic lease acquisition/renewal;expired lease is reclaimable without duplicate committed side effects;bounded backoff and retry budget terminate in dead-letter with evidence;crash cannot leave permanent processing. PRIORITY-5-AUDIT:gptbridge_audit.event is append-only for runtime identities;runtime UPDATE/DELETE is denied. Each event records monotonic sequence,event_id,module_id,occurred_at,correlation_id,actor/action,target,result,previous_event_hash and event_hash or an approved batch digest with equivalent tamper evidence. Corrections append successor events. SQLite audit remains local module-operation evidence and never replaces central audit. PRIORITY-6-RUST-VECTOR-ENGINE:Rust-Vector-Engine contains no unique business truth. PostgreSQL retains resource/chunk source text or canonical locator,ordering,metadata,ACL/classification,content hashes,embedding model/version and pipeline state sufficient to recreate every point and mapping after total loss. Snapshot restore and clean rebuild must be verified against manifest counts/hashes and retrieval parity. PRIORITY-7-SQLITE-FLEET:every governed SQLite database declares schema_version,module_id,database_role,created_at,last_migrated_at,integrity_hash,reconcile_state plus owner,path code and retention;registry covers every database,prevents role drift and runs integrity/migration/reconciliation evidence without treating file count as failure. PRIORITY-8-RECOVERY:PostgreSQL uses logical backup plus WAL/point-in-time consistency verification;SQLite uses transaction-consistent file snapshot plus integrity_check and restore test;Rust-Vector-Engine uses snapshot or deterministic rebuild verification. Recovery manifests bind revision,resource range,hash,encryption/retention,RPO/RTO,restore result and cross-store reconciliation. ORDER:priorities are binding sequencing;backup does not compensate for unresolved identity or reconciliation defects. FAILURE-ISOLATION:a failed store/channel is isolated;unaffected stores continue;pending durable work remains bounded and observable;no repair may overwrite/reset canonical source or code.

The binding dependency order is exactly: 1 RECONCILIATION(PostgreSQL<->SQLite authority/revision/hash/status); 2 GLOBAL_ID_VERSION(one resource_id and version contract across PostgreSQL,SQLite,Rust-Vector-Engine); 3 CENTRAL_INDEX(measured PostgreSQL indexes over stable identities); 4 TRANSPORT(durable lease,idempotency,retry,deadline,dead-letter); 5 AUDIT(central append-only sequence/hash/correlation evidence); 6 RUST-VECTOR-ENGINE_REBUILD(PostgreSQL-backed deterministic complete reconstruction); 7 SQLITE_GOVERNANCE(fleet registry,schema/role/integrity/reconcile state); 8 BACKUP_RECOVERY(PostgreSQL WAL/logical,SQLite snapshot/integrity,Rust-Vector-Engine snapshot or rebuild and cross-store restore proof). Each stage consumes verified evidence from every preceding stage. A later stage may be designed or tested in isolation but cannot be declared complete,authoritative,release-ready or used to waive an earlier incomplete stage. Failure at stage N blocks activation of N and every downstream stage while already verified upstream services remain available and the failure is isolated. Re-entry after repair resumes from the earliest invalid stage and revalidates all downstream evidence. The synchronization sovereign coordinates runtime transport and reconciliation;permission sovereign governs directory/access boundaries;neither changes PostgreSQL central authority,SQLite bounded role or Rust-Vector-Engine projection role.

POOL-ISOLATION:central-index,transport,audit and each module-private database use separately budgeted connection pools with owner,max/open/idle/wait/lease metrics and reserved critical capacity;one workload cannot exhaust another pool. READ-WRITE-PATH:code exposes distinct read and write paths even on one host;transaction consistency and read-after-write requirements are explicit and routing may later change without contract drift. SQL-SAFETY:all runtime values use prepared statements or parameterized queries;SQL string concatenation/interpolation for transport,locator,resource lookup and every runtime query is prohibited. TIMEOUTS:every runtime statement has a bounded statement_timeout;transactions have lock_timeout,idle timeout and bounded deadlock/serialization retry with jitter,idempotency and total deadline;retry never duplicates committed side effects. PERFORMANCE-EVIDENCE:slow-query log stores redacted query digest,role/module,mean,p95,p99,rows examined/returned,calls and plan identity without secrets or raw personal values. Periodic analysis identifies unused/duplicate indexes and abnormal sequential scans;index removal/addition requires workload,query-plan,write/storage and rollback evidence. RETENTION:audit,transport history,model inference history and repair history each declare retention,archive/legal-hold,purge owner and proof;central append-only audit uses governed archival/purge rather than runtime mutation. VACUUM-ANALYZE:Python health/maintenance orchestration observes bloat,dead tuples,statistics freshness and transaction age,then schedules bounded VACUUM/ANALYZE through governed execution;manual recurring dependence is forbidden. SCHEMA-CONTRACT:startup verifies expected schema version,tables,columns/types/nullability,constraints,indexes,RLS/policies,extensions and migration head before write readiness. DRIFT:actual catalog is deterministically compared to approved migration-derived schema digest;out-of-band change becomes SCHEMA_DRIFT,blocks unsafe writes and cannot be silently adopted. MIGRATION-DRY-RUN:before formal migration validate dependency graph,lock/table-rewrite risk,name/type/default conflicts,data conversion,space/time budget,upgrade order,rollback or downgrade feasibility and mixed-version compatibility;destructive or irreversible steps require explicit evidence and user/governance authorization. MODULE-DB-HEALTH:each module database state is exactly healthy|degraded|reconcile_required|read_only|failed with reason,evidence,time and allowed operations;health state does not change authority. LOCATOR:verify locator target identity,existence,boundary and content/version hash;missing or mismatched target is orphaned and is never returned as valid. TOMBSTONE:resource deletion first writes deleted/tombstoned status,revision,time,actor,reason and correlation_id;downstream cleanup and audit complete before policy-governed purge;hard delete cannot erase required lineage. VECTOR-FRESHNESS:compare point resource_id/chunk_id/resource_version/content_hash/embedding version to PostgreSQL;older or mismatched vector is stale,excluded from authoritative retrieval and queued for idempotent rebuild. SQLITE-WAL:monitor WAL bytes/age,checkpoint progress,busy_timeout,reader/writer age and database-locked rate;checkpoint is bounded and cannot truncate active work. SQLite integrity checks are risk-based/rotating and cover the fleet within a declared maximum interval;startup does not synchronously scan every database unless incident evidence requires it. CENTRAL-SHAPE:central index stores necessary normalized frequently queried fields;JSONB is for bounded typed extension data with schema,size/index/retention rules and cannot become an unbounded catch-all. CROSS-ENGINE-EVENT:every SQLite>PostgreSQL and PostgreSQL>Rust-Vector-Engine transition uses one correlation_id with resource_id,from/to revision,hash,status,idempotency key and audit linkage across the entire chain. All controls obey the A367 stage order.

PLATFORM:PostgreSQL central official structured authority,SQLite module-private bounded state and Rust-Vector-Engine canonical semantic projection operate as one observable,verifiable,recoverable local data platform;Rust-Vector-Engine remains fully rebuildable and is never unique business truth. HEALTH-CENTER:one normalized health center covers PostgreSQL,every SQLite module database,Rust-Vector-Engine,Migration,Reconcile,Locator,RLS and Index. Every component emits exactly healthy|degraded|stale|reconcile_required|failed plus component_id,resource/module scope,observed revision,expected revision,evidence,reason,first/last observed time,allowed operations and correlation_id. Local aliases are forbidden at the platform boundary. Health aggregation preserves every component finding;one healthy component cannot mask another failed/stale component. CONSISTENCY:auto-check SQLite resource revision/content_hash against PostgreSQL resource revision/content_hash and Rust-Vector-Engine vector resource_version/content_hash/embedding version. Any mismatch immediately becomes stale or reconcile_required according to authority and blocks authoritative use;it creates evidence and never silently overwrites,promotes or deletes either side. RECOVERY-STATE-MACHINE:all data faults use detect>isolate>retry>reconcile>verify>recover>audit. Transitions are explicit,idempotent,deadline/retry bounded and correlation-preserving;skip/reorder is forbidden. Recover requires post-reconcile identity/revision/hash/schema/behavior proof;failure remains isolated/fail-closed and reaches audit. RESOURCE-LIFECYCLE:each resource state is exactly active|stale|superseded|tombstoned|archived|purged with revision,time,actor,reason,predecessor/successor and audit linkage. Legal transitions are active>stale>active after verified reconcile;active/stale>superseded;tombstoned only before archived/purged;purged is terminal and permitted only after retention,reference,backup and audit gates. Direct DELETE cannot bypass lifecycle. SQL-OBSERVABILITY:central performance telemetry records redacted query_digest,duration,mean,p95,p99,lock_wait,rows_scanned,rows_returned,index_usage,pool_usage,module/role and time window;budgets trigger degraded/failed health and measured remediation,not automatic index churn. MIGRATION-RELEASE:formal sequence is validate>dry-run>backup-checkpoint>migrate>schema-verify>RLS-verify>smoke-test>promote. Every step binds migration/version/hash,dependencies,lock/space/time risk and evidence. Before promote any failure performs an approved safe rollback when provably reversible;otherwise fail-closed/read-only with recovery evidence. No partially verified schema is write-ready. SCHEMA-DRIFT:compare migration-derived expected schema to actual PostgreSQL tables,columns,constraints,indexes,RLS/policies/extensions and migration head;difference immediately alerts,marks degraded/failed,blocks unsafe writes and cannot be accepted without an explicit migration. RUST-VECTOR-ENGINE-REBUILD:PostgreSQL plus registered private canonical source data deterministically produces resource>chunk>embedding>Rust-Vector-Engine using versioned pipeline,model and manifests;total-loss rebuild verifies counts,IDs,versions,hashes,ACL and retrieval parity. SQLITE-FLEET:one registry tracks every SQLite database schema_version,WAL bytes/age/checkpoint,busy/lock state,integrity,size,last_backup,last_reconcile,last_migration,health and owner;checks are risk-ranked and rotating with declared maximum coverage interval. BACKUP-VERIFICATION:every backup class must regularly execute backup>isolated restore-test>engine integrity-check>cross-store consistency verification>result audit. A backup without successful current restore evidence is unverified and cannot satisfy recovery readiness. ORDER:all controls remain subordinate to A367 exact stage order.

PURPOSE:PostgreSQL central official structured authority,SQLite module-private operation state and Rust-Vector-Engine canonical rebuildable semantic projection form a self-observing,self-diagnosing,controlled-self-optimizing local platform;no new database technology is implied. INDEX-OPTIMIZATION:collect redacted slow-query digests and comparable plans;analyze sequential scans,index scans,selectivity,rows,frequency,write cost and table size;detect unused and duplicate indexes;produce an evidence-bound recommendation. Creation follows recommend>dry-run/EXPLAIN>lock/write/storage budget>approval under automatic repair/update user-confirmation rules>controlled create>plan/performance verification>audit. Runtime programs cannot arbitrarily DROP indexes;drop requires explicit governed proposal,dependency/constraint check,rollback plan,observation window and user confirmation. CAPACITY:measure PostgreSQL table/index,SQLite database/WAL and Rust-Vector-Engine collection growth rates with retention-aware baselines;forecast 30/90/180-day bytes and exhaustion date with confidence/assumptions;crossing budget triggers archive or maintenance proposal early,never silent destructive cleanup. DATA-TIERS:resource tier is Hot(recent/high-frequency),Warm(normal history),Archive(long retention),Tombstone(awaiting governed cleanup),Purged(formally removed). Tier transitions preserve resource lifecycle,revision,locator,ACL,retention,correlation and audit;access frequency alone cannot override legal hold or authority. QUERY-BUDGET:each SQL workload class declares statement timeout,max rows/bytes,max transaction duration,max retry,max lock wait,pool allocation and priority;enforcement fails boundedly and isolates the offending module so one workload cannot exhaust central PostgreSQL. BACKPRESSURE:gptbridge_transport pressure state is exactly normal>throttled>degraded>reject-low-priority with thresholds,hysteresis,queue/lease age,capacity and recovery criteria. High-priority accepted work remains bounded;low-priority rejection is explicit,retry-after capable and audited;no infinite enqueue or retry storm. FAULT-INJECTION:regular isolated tests stop PostgreSQL,stop Rust-Vector-Engine,lock SQLite,expand WAL,interrupt migration,invalidate locator,misconfigure RLS and exhaust a connection pool;verify fail-closed,degradation,isolation,backpressure,reconciliation and unaffected continuity. RECOVERY-DRILL:periodically execute fault>fail-closed>degrade>restore>reconcile>Rust-Vector-Engine rebuild>integrity verify>reopen;reopen requires verified schema/RLS,resource revisions/content hashes,audit continuity and recovery objectives,not merely process availability. INTEGRITY-SUMMARY:each data domain periodically emits resource_count,revision_head,content_hash/schema digest,schema_version,reconcile_generation,audit_sequence,backend_generation and evidence time;differences become stale/reconcile_required and cannot be hidden by a score. GENERATION:one monotonic backend_generation is shared in PostgreSQL,registered SQLite and Rust-Vector-Engine manifests;major rebuild/restore increments it once through a coordinated generation transaction. Every record/projection binds its producing generation;prior-generation vectors or state are stale until verified or rebuilt. SCORING:each engine/fleet may expose 0..100 Health,Consistency,Performance,Recoverability,Security scores with formula,input freshness and confidence. Scores are monitoring summaries only,never governance authority,never suppress findings and never authorize mutation/reopen/release. LOOP:database>monitor>detect anomaly>diagnose>propose optimization>user-confirmed controlled execution>verify>audit. All execution observes A366 confirmation,A367 stage order,A368 controls and A369 health/recovery contracts.

DEFAULT-PATH:when Rust-Vector-Engine and PostgreSQL pass readiness,authorization,schema/version and health gates,the mandatory normal RAG path is source content>qwen3-embedding:4b 2560-dimensional embedding>Rust-Vector-Engine dense retrieval plus PostgreSQL FTS/metadata filtering>RRF>reranker. LocalVectorStore and LocalSqliteRagRepository are bounded-degraded fallback only and cannot remain the preferred/default route while canonical services are healthy. Runtime reports canonical=true only after live-path evidence proves both canonical stores and reconciliation complete;fixed canonical=false/reconciliation_required=true presentation is forbidden when state differs. DEGRADATION:only a verified Rust-Vector-Engine or PostgreSQL failure/unavailability/unsafe state may route affected scope to LocalVectorStore 256-dimensional hashing n-gram/fallback plus LocalSqliteRagRepository. Degradation is explicit,correlation-bound,time/budget limited and preserves resource_id,locator_id,source revision/content hash and pending reconciliation;it never changes authority. RECONCILIATION:degraded vectors are never copied,dimension-padded,projected or treated as canonical embeddings. Recovery pipeline is degraded resource_id+locator_id>authorized owning-module source resolution>source revision and SHA256 verification>canonical code/content chunking>qwen3-embedding:4b>new 2560D vector>Rust-Vector-Engine upsert with idempotency/generation>PostgreSQL index_state update>cross-store verification>reconciliation_required=false>audit. Missing/changed source,hash mismatch,model/dimension mismatch or partial write remains conflict/stale and fail-closed. FOUR-RAG-BEHAVIORS:hybrid-rag executes dense+keyword+RRF+reranker. code-rag additionally requires language-aware AST,symbol/declaration/reference,dependency graph,file/module relation and code-specific chunk boundaries with source-revision evidence. agentic-rag requires bounded retrieve>inspect evidence>reformulate>retrieve again loop with iteration/deadline/budget,novelty/progress test,stop condition and cited evidence;it cannot self-authorize tools or bypass retrieval ACL. memory-rag requires session,long-term and episodic separation,recency/decay policy,memory scope,identity/consent/retention and cross-session authorization;it cannot mix another identity/module scope. A shared engine may provide common primitives,but each rag_type must demonstrate its distinct execution behavior and tests;four declarations over one undifferentiated hybrid behavior are noncompliant. SHARED-COLLECTION:gptbridge_shared_knowledge is the single canonical shared Rust-Vector-Engine collection for authorized local models unless a later special law changes it;do not create per-model duplicate indexes. Each point records point_id,locator_id,resource_id,chunk_id,module_id,rag_type or governed rag_types,data_category,resource_type,classification,embedding_model,embedding_version,resource/version,content_hash,backend_generation and pipeline version. Filtering by module,classification,rag type and authorization occurs before content resolution. OPAQUE-SECURITY:Rust-Vector-Engine cannot store content,text,path,physical_location,windows_path,secrets or independently resolvable physical locations. It stores opaque locator and metadata only;RagAuthorizationBridge and owning module resolve content after authorization. PostgreSQL/private source retains rebuild truth. HEALTH:Rust-Vector-Engine total loss rebuilds from PostgreSQL manifests plus owning-module source,never from degraded 256D vectors.

The binding local RAG work and activation order is exactly: 1 RUST_VECTOR_CANONICAL_RUNTIME makes healthy Rust-Vector-Engine the proven default dense read/write execution path and confines LocalVectorStore to bounded degradation; 2 POSTGRESQL_CENTRAL_METADATA makes PostgreSQL the official metadata,FTS,index_state,resource/chunk/version and locator-mapping authority used by the live path; 3 DEGRADED_RECONCILIATION proves end-to-end fallback capture,owning-source resolution,re-chunk,SHA256 verification,2560D re-embedding,Rust-Vector-Engine upsert,PostgreSQL state update and reconciliation closure without copying 256D vectors; 4 CODE_RAG implements and verifies AST,symbol,dependency,file/module and code-chunk behavior; 5 AGENTIC_RAG implements bounded evidence inspection,reformulation,retrieval iteration and stop conditions; 6 MEMORY_RAG implements session,long-term,episodic,recency,scope,identity,consent and retention behavior. Each stage consumes current passing evidence from all predecessors. A later stage may be researched or tested in isolation but cannot be declared complete,default,production-ready or release-blocking until every predecessor is active and verified. Failure/staleness at stage N blocks activation of N through 6;verified upstream capability remains available and the fault is isolated. After correction,revalidation resumes at the earliest invalid stage and refreshes every dependent downstream result. Hybrid RAG remains the common retrieval foundation but cannot be used to claim completion of Code,Agentic or Memory behavior.

CANONICAL-TAKEOVER:normal read/write execution must prove Rust-Vector-Engine dense retrieval and PostgreSQL official metadata/FTS/index_state are the live path;LocalVectorStore and LocalSqliteRagRepository activate only for the affected scope after canonical unavailability/unsafe-state evidence. Application code cannot select local fallback merely by default configuration or convenience. RECONCILIATION-QUEUE:every degraded create,update,tombstone,archive or permission/version change creates one durable item with operation_id,idempotency_key,resource_id,locator_id,source_revision,content_hash,operation,tombstone_generation,required embedding/chunk/parser/schema versions,created_at,attempts,next_retry_at,deadline,status,correlation_id and last_error. Status is pending|leased|reconciling|verified|conflict|failed|dead_letter;boolean reconciliation_required is only a projection and never the queue. Lease/retry/dead-letter rules follow Transport governance. CROSS-STORE-WRITE:no unsafe best-effort dual write. A logical operation uses an outbox/saga equivalent:commit central intent and operation identity;apply Rust-Vector-Engine and PostgreSQL idempotently;record each store result;compensate or reconcile partial success;publish complete only after revision/hash/tombstone parity. Rust-Vector-Engine success/PostgreSQL failure and the reverse remain visible recoverable incomplete states,never reported successful. TOMBSTONE-ANTI-RESURRECTION:delete writes authoritative PostgreSQL tombstone with monotonic resource revision and tombstone_generation before vector cleanup;queue and Rust-Vector-Engine payload carry it. Reconciliation rejects any older create/update/vector and cannot recreate a point from stale degraded state. Purge occurs only after all consumers acknowledge tombstone and retention/audit gates pass. INDEX-VERSION:each resource/chunk/point records embedding_model+embedding_version+dimension,chunker_version,parser_version,schema_version,pipeline_version,source_revision,content_hash and backend_generation. Version change calculates affected scope and precisely marks stale/rebuild;no global rebuild when narrower proof suffices,and no partial reuse across incompatible versions. DUAL-AUTHORIZATION:before Rust-Vector-Engine query enforce server-side module_id plus classification/rag_type filters from authorized scope;after results return,RagAuthorizationBridge revalidates caller,module,locator,classification,resource revision and current permission before content resolution. Either denial removes result and is audited without leaking metadata. OBSERVABILITY:each request reports mode=canonical|degraded|reconciling and per-stage path/status/latency/fallback reason for embedding,Rust-Vector-Engine,PostgreSQL FTS/metadata,RRF,reranker,authorization and content resolution;aggregate health cannot hide stage fallback. RETRIEVAL-EVALUATION:versioned fixed question/corpus sets measure Recall@K,MRR,reranker lift,grounded-answer evidence/citation validity,authorization leakage,latency and fallback parity. Dataset/version/expected relevant IDs,scoring tolerance and baseline are immutable evidence;regression policy blocks promotion. AGENTIC-BUDGET:per request bound retrieval rounds,model calls,total tokens/tool calls,deadline,candidate count and no-progress repetitions;stop on sufficient evidence,budget/deadline,no progress or explicit cancellation. MEMORY-LIFECYCLE:session,episodic,long-term memories have distinct scope,retention,consent,promotion/update/supersession/forget and retrieval-recency rules;no automatic cross-scope promotion. CODE-STRUCTURE:Code RAG indexes AST node type,symbol/declaration/reference,imports/includes,dependency edges,file/module/build relation and code-specific chunk spans with language/parser/source revision;plain-text chunks alone cannot satisfy Code RAG. All activation follows A372 order.

INDEX-STATE:every indexed resource/chunk has an authoritative index_state recording at minimum embedding_model,embedding_dimension,chunk_size,chunk_overlap,chunking_version,parser_version,rag_schema_version,content_sha256,indexed_at plus resource_id,chunk_id,source_revision,pipeline_version,backend_generation and status. Reindex planning compares each field and marks only the exact affected resources/chunks stale. A change such as chunk_size 1200/overlap 200 to 1600/250 invalidates entries built under the old pair and their dependent chunk/point mappings;it does not authorize deleting/rebuilding unrelated compatible data or the entire collection. STATE-MACHINE:runtime RAG state is exactly CANONICAL,DEGRADED or RECONCILING. CANONICAL requires healthy Rust-Vector-Engine and PostgreSQL,matching index_state and complete queue. Verified Rust-Vector-Engine/PostgreSQL fault moves affected scope to DEGRADED;bounded SQLite/local-vector service may continue,each mutation is durably queued and reconciliation_required=true. Canonical recovery moves to RECONCILING,which must verify source SHA256,resolve owning-module original content,re-chunk under current index_state,re-embed with canonical model/dimension,idempotently write Rust-Vector-Engine,update PostgreSQL,verify resource/chunk/point counts+IDs+hashes+versions and drain/close queue. Only then may reconciliation_required=false and state return CANONICAL. Service availability alone cannot transition to CANONICAL;SQLite vectors are never copied as canonical. COLLECTION-TOPOLOGY:one Rust-Vector-Engine instance and one canonical collection gptbridge_shared_knowledge serve all authorized local models and four RAG behaviors. Physical per-rag-type or per-model canonical collections are forbidden. Logical isolation uses governed point metadata rag_type with one value or rag_types array containing only hybrid-rag,code-rag,agentic-rag,memory-rag;server-side metadata filters and post-result authorization apply. A chunk may carry multiple rag_types only when each membership has evidence and compatible lifecycle/version. RERANKER-OBSERVABILITY:every retrieval response/evidence reports reranker.requested,reranker.active,reranker.fallback,reranker.reason,model/version and timing. If qwen3-reranker-0.6b is unavailable/not cached,the lawful fallback is RRF with active=false,fallback=rrf and a typed reason such as model_not_cached;successful response cannot imply reranker participation. ORDER:this provision supersedes the shorter A372 work order with the binding sequence:1 Canonical Rust-Vector-Engine;2 PostgreSQL canonical metadata;3 recoverable cross-store write consistency;4 reconciliation;5 index versioning;6 dual-layer authorization filtering;7 stage observability including reranker;8 Code RAG;9 Agentic RAG;10 Memory RAG;11 retrieval benchmark. All project query,index,repair and knowledge workflows use the DAG,CAG,RAG hybrid architecture. DAG is the orchestration plane and never replaces RagApplicationService;the sole planner and executor are RagDagPlanner and RagDagExecutor. CAG is the scoped,versioned,leased acceleration and context-reuse plane and never replaces RAG or creates authority. RAG is the canonical retrieval plane and retains Hybrid,Code,Memory and Agentic sub-architectures. The request path is Caller>Information Channel>Permission and Scope>RagApplicationService>DAG Planner and Executor>CAG Gate>RAG Retrieval>Evidence Fusion>Reranker>Context Builder>Local LLM>Citation Validation>Result. AUTOMATIC-MAINTENANCE:source revision,lifecycle,permission,contract,embedding,reranker,chunking,collection and deletion events trigger a bounded maintenance DAG;periodic full reconciliation is low-frequency compensation only. Maintenance validates sources,chunks and hashes content,performs incremental index upsert,tombstone,orphan scanning,PostgreSQL-Rust-Vector-Engine reconciliation,CAG invalidation,collection optimization,snapshot verification and necessary rebuild. AUTHORITY:PostgreSQL owns official structured knowledge metadata,source revision,locator,permission and publication state;Rust-Vector-Engine is a scoped derived semantic index;CAG is derived cache;SQLite is owner-private bounded degraded state only. PUBLICATION:new generations pass PREPARING>INDEXING>VERIFYING>READY and only READY is readable;failure yields REQUIRES_RECONCILE or QUARANTINED and preserves the last verified generation. DELETION:follows tombstone,retention,reference check,PostgreSQL state update,Rust-Vector-Engine point removal and CAG invalidation;unknown references preserve data. RESOURCES:interactive retrieval preempts background maintenance;each DAG declares deadline,concurrency,CPU,memory,GPU,batch,cancellation and retry bounds. EVIDENCE:each run records source set,generation,content and index roots,count parity,orphans,invalidations,latency,resources,error class and publication result. CAG-AUTOMATIC-MAINTENANCE:cache entries are created on demand only and bind entry identity,caller and module scope,permission and identity generation,source revision roots,contract version,model,prompt,chunking,embedding,reranker and citation-policy versions,content digest,created and accessed times,lease,TTL,byte size and lifecycle status. Every lookup passes CAG Gate validation of scope,permission generation,source roots,all policy versions,lease,expiry and digest before reuse;any mismatch is a cache miss,immediate invalidation and canonical RAG retrieval,never degraded acceptance. Source change,permission revocation,identity-generation raise,contract/model/prompt/chunking/embedding/reranker/citation-policy change,tombstone or deletion emits a scoped invalidation event. Capacity is bounded per scope and workload by entry,byte and age ceilings;eligible derived entries may be evicted by expiry and bounded recency policy. Maintenance performs invalidation propagation,orphan scan,lease cleanup,size enforcement,digest verification and cache-to-source reconciliation and records a CAG maintenance receipt. No unsolicited pre-warm,unlimited retention,cross-scope reuse or hit-rate-based correctness claim is permitted. DAG-AUTOMATIC-MAINTENANCE:DAG definitions are immutable versioned generations. Before publication the sole RagDagPlanner and RagDagExecutor validate graph identity,node and edge types,acyclicity,input/output contracts,dependency closure,scope,permission,deadline,cancellation,resource budgets,retry classes,idempotency and compensation policy;only a complete generation may switch atomically to current. Source,contract,capability,permission,model or policy changes invalidate affected plans and trigger bounded recompilation and validation. Executions bind generation,operation and correlation identities,lease,deadline,attempt budget and checkpoints. A crashed process or expired lease may resume only from a verified checkpoint;unknown effects require lookup and verification before retry,compensation,invalidation,reconciliation or quarantine. Maintenance detects cycles,missing nodes,orphan edges,stale generations,expired leases,abandoned executions,checkpoint drift and resource-budget violations. Completed,cancelled,failed and expired execution artifacts are cleaned only after retention and reference checks;in-flight,referred or indeterminate artifacts are preserved. Every graph build,switch,recovery,compensation and cleanup emits a typed receipt;no node may create authority or execute raw shell,SQL,Rust-Vector-Engine or filesystem operations.

Development source and production runtime are separated: coding agents edit the working tree while the production system executes from runtime/releases/release-A or release-B. A release must contain backend code, shared runtime dependencies, required contracts, the dependency lock and build metadata - otherwise a development shared-layer can still be imported even when main-system is pinned.
PostgreSQL data, Rust-Vector-Engine indexes, model weights and user data must not be copied per release.
registered Codex contract section 10.19 records the layout and contents; runtime/releases and the release packaging do not exist (gap G57).

Connection layer hardening on the existing React -> Electron Main -> Backend Gateway -> Request Registry -> Python Backend path: connection states CONNECTING/CONNECTED/RECONNECTING/DISCONNECTED/CLOSED where DISCONNECTED is temporary and CLOSED forbids further auto-reconnects, with connection state kept separate from backend lifecycle state (ACTIVE plus RECONNECTING may hold simultaneously); bounded exponential backoff with jitter, maximum interval, connect timeout, single WebSocket and single reconnect loop, no reconnect after formal shutdown, authentication and handshake re-verified on every reconnect, and no automatic re-execution of unconfirmed non-idempotent operations; on disconnect the request registry is never cleared and each request is judged by state (COMPLETED/CANCELLED never re-run, RUNNING checks the original backend, QUEUED follows persistence and execution eligibility) with no cross-backend migration in this phase.
Streaming keeps per-request sequences (request_id/backend_generation/sequence/event_type reused with backward-compatible extension), recognises duplicate/expired/out-of-order/gap events, never re-applies applied events and never duplicates tokens after reconnect; buffers are bounded with congestion detection, never silently drop completion events, never merge different requests and safely terminate or mark the stream when the bound is insufficient; the existing heartbeat is reused and distinguishes transport-liveness, backend-process-liveness, backend READY and backend DEGRADED (a connected WebSocket does not mean the system is healthy and a degraded Rust-Vector-Engine does not force a disconnect); the UI is not redesigned and no second global UI state store is created; the gateway transports connections and events only and never authorises execution, reconnect never bypasses authentication and codex checks, and tokens/passwords/credentials never appear in debug logs; this phase may only modify the existing gateway, WebSocket client, request registry, the necessary event and connection-state contracts and their tests. Acceptance requires seventeen cases in an isolated test backend (normal connect; reconnect when the backend is not started; temporary disconnect after connect; recovery; repeated disconnects; shutdown during reconnect; concurrent requests; streaming interruption; duplicate, expired and out-of-order streaming events; cancellation racing reconnect; backend exited but gateway unaware; authentication re-run on reconnect; legacy IPC compatibility; buffer at capacity; backend completed but the response was lost without blindly redoing non-idempotent work); the running production backend must never be interrupted or modified.
registered Codex contract section 10.26 records the specification; none of the connection-state, reconnect, backpressure or heartbeat distinctions are implemented (gap G63).
